target.title: RFC: add local adaptive-refresh replay tooling
target.body:
## Decision requested

Should CodexBar upstream own an offline CLI for comparing refresh policies against a caller-supplied JSONL trace?

The supporting `AdaptiveReplayKit` target is package-internal. This PR adds one executable product, `AdaptiveReplayCLI`. It does not change Adaptive, make it the default, or add a production signal.

Refs #1739 and #1861.

## Scope after review

Copilot and ClawSweeper identified two concrete problems in the previous revision: CRLF records were not parsed correctly, and the branch mixed offline analysis with runtime collection and transcript metadata access.

This revision is rebased onto current `main` and narrows the diff from 32 files and +4,147/-55 to 21 files and +2,840/-7. It removes:

- app-side trace recording and every `Sources/CodexBar` hook;
- transcript-directory scanning and activity collection;
- the persistent trace writer and storage contract;
- recorder, writer, and activity-probe tests;
- the unrelated Keychain test adjustment.

There are no changes under `Sources/CodexBar`, and the app target's dependencies are unchanged. Of the 2,840 additions, 1,516 are the offline implementation, 1,224 are tests, and 100 are package or documentation changes.

The remaining code is:

- a Foundation-only schema, strict and tolerant JSONL parsers, replay engine, policy models, segmentation, metrics, and schedule audit;
- a package-internal library target and one CLI product;
- six platform-independent test files plus a macOS-only parity test against the production Adaptive policy;
- an evidence-only update to the existing decision record.

The parser now splits records with `Character.isNewline`, which handles Swift's CRLF grapheme correctly. Strict and tolerant multi-record CRLF regression tests cover the two Copilot findings.

## Data boundary

The CLI reads an explicit trace path and writes a report to stdout. This PR has no app-side recorder, trace writer, storage lifecycle, transcript scanning or collection, provider calls, network path, or production-policy change. Optional activity fields are input-only. No trace or fixture is committed.

Runtime capture and its privacy/lifecycle contract are deliberately out of scope and can be proposed separately if the offline tool is accepted.

## Author-run replay evidence

Exact head: `cd96204ac197ec0c7ce48e615a608358c01ba3fb`

The local input has 1,780 records and SHA-256 `b1e4aa33180b7c177293eb9ed16b45e24e026d259600fba2b1b67b931b904f0b`. The raw trace remains local.

| Policy | Simulated refreshes | Per observed 24h | Simulated advances | Unconstrained active over 5m | Menu staleness p50 / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Current Adaptive | 694 | 143.47 | 53 | 4 / 145 | 142s / 1093s |
| Activity-cap candidate | 696 | 143.88 | 53 | 0 / 145 | 139s / 1093s |
| Fixed 5m | 1,383 | 285.90 | 0 | 0 / 99 | 150s / 281s |

The run found 28 observed segments and excluded 26.10 hours with a five-minute legacy-gap heuristic. Activity fields were present for 462 of 733 decisions; 185 of those 462 samples were inside the five-minute active window. The trace contains 46 recorded advances and zero timer-advance evaluations.

On this input, current Adaptive schedules 49.8% fewer simulated refreshes than fixed five minutes. The candidate adds two refreshes and removes four active-delay violations, but neither Adaptive variant improves p95 staleness. This supports evaluating the tooling; it does not support a default or production-policy change.

## Validation

For exact head `cd96204a`:

- `make check` passed: SwiftFormat 0/1,372 and SwiftLint 0 violations in 1,371 files.
- `swift package describe` exposes `AdaptiveReplayCLI` but not `AdaptiveReplayKit` as a product.
- `swift build --product AdaptiveReplayCLI` passed.
- `swift run AdaptiveReplayCLI <hash-pinned-trace>` produced the table above and the segmentation/audit totals.

The direct parent `d394420d`, with identical source and test code, passed the full 610 selections in 51/51 groups, 54 offline replay tests, 16 parser tests, and 3 production-policy parity tests. The only change in `cd96204a` is removing the public `AdaptiveReplayKit` product declaration. Upstream CI is running the exact head.

## Limitations

- This is author-run evidence from one machine, not an independently reproducible dataset.
- Gap segmentation is heuristic and cannot identify sleep, reboot, a long refresh, or an event-loop stall.
- The trace predates evaluation records, so accepted versus rejected live evaluations cannot be audited.
- The result does not measure battery use, elapsed user time, provider requests, or cost.
- Both Adaptive variants have worse p95 menu staleness than fixed five minutes on this trace.

The review question is intentionally narrow: should this repository own the offline CLI and its package-internal replay target?

target.title: Fix Gemini OAuth refresh when CLI oauth2.js is missing
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #1978.

When Gemini access tokens expire, CodexBar must read OAuth client credentials from the installed Gemini CLI. If `oauth2.js` cannot be found, refresh failed early with `Could not find Gemini CLI OAuth configuration` before Google could return the consumer-tier migration signals handled by #1931.

This adds broader OAuth client discovery and clearer recovery guidance.

## Changes

- Add `GeminiOAuthConfig` env helpers for `GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `GEMINI_OAUTH2_JS_PATH`
- Resolve OAuth client credentials in order: env override → installed CLI → explicit oauth2.js path → known Homebrew/npm global install paths → Homebrew Cellar/`opt` `libexec` package roots
- Isolate OAuth env overrides via `@TaskLocal` so parallel Gemini suites cannot pick leaked process-wide credentials
- Replace the opaque missing-config error with combined Gemini CLI repair + Antigravity migration guidance for consumer accounts, while noting Workspace/education accounts should keep using Gemini
- Add fixture-backed API/config tests (including no-binary Homebrew Cellar discovery) and update `docs/gemini.md`

## Testing

- `swift test --filter 'GeminiOAuthConfigTests|GeminiOAuthRecoveryAPITests'` (5/5 passed)
- `swiftformat` + `swiftlint --strict` on changed files

## Live proof (redacted)

Verified on 2026-07-08 against PR head `20e709312` with a real `~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json` that still had a refresh token.

**Setup shared by both runs**
- Forced access token to an expired marker and set `expiry_date` in the past
- Pointed `GEMINI_CLI_PATH` at a fake `gemini` binary that has **no** `oauth2.js` / OAuth client constants
- Used debug CLI: `.build/debug/CodexBarCLI usage --provider gemini --format json --pretty --status`
- Secrets/emails redacted below; no client secret pasted

### Proof 1 — `GEMINI_OAUTH2_JS_PATH` recovery

```text
GEMINI_CLI_PATH=<fake-gemini-without-oauth>
GEMINI_OAUTH2_JS_PATH=/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@google/gemini-cli/node_modules/@google/gemini-cli-core/dist/src/code_assist/oauth2.js
.build/debug/CodexBarCLI usage --provider gemini --format json --pretty --status
exit_code=0
```

Redacted stdout:

```json
[
  {
    "provider" : "gemini",
    "source" : "oauth-api",
    "usage" : {
      "accountEmail" : "<redacted-email>",
      "identity" : {
        "accountEmail" : "<redacted-email>",
        "loginMethod" : "Paid",
        "providerID" : "gemini"
      },
      "loginMethod" : "Paid",
      "primary" : {
        "resetDescription" : "Resets in 23h 59m",
        "usedPercent" : 0,
        "windowMinutes" : 1440
      },
      "updatedAt" : "2026-07-08T14:11:08Z"
    }
  }
]
```

Post-run credential check: access token no longer the expired marker; `expiry_date` is in the future; `refresh_succeeded=true`.

### Proof 2 — known install-path recovery (no oauth2 path / client env)

Same expired credential + fake CLI, with `GEMINI_OAUTH2_JS_PATH` / `GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_*` unset so discovery must use known Homebrew/npm install paths:

```text
GEMINI_CLI_PATH=<fake-gemini-without-oauth>
unset GEMINI_OAUTH2_JS_PATH GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
.build/debug/CodexBarCLI usage --provider gemini --format json --pretty --status
exit_code=0
provider=gemini source=oauth-api loginMethod=Paid usedPercent=0
refresh_succeeded=true
```

Both proofs show the new recovery path can refresh past a missing in-CLI `oauth2.js` layout without the old `Could not find Gemini CLI OAuth configuration` dead-end.

## Related

- Complements #1980 (Gemini plan display via `paidTier.name` for #1972)
- Builds on #1931 consumer-tier migration handling

target.title: fix: revert unsafe Pi cumulative reconciliation
target.body:
## Summary

- revert the unreleased Pi cumulative-reconciliation change from #2043
- restore the exact pre-merge scanner, tests, cache formula, and changelog state
- keep #2037 canonical for a later cross-file redesign against a sanitized real fork corpus

## Why revert

The merged implementation reconciles rows inside each session file, so copied ancestor rows across fork files remain duplicated and the reported root cause is still present. Independent generic fixtures also reproduced two new undercount paths: distinct events collapsing under a broader shared lineage, and cumulative token deltas being priced without the full nonlinear context.

A narrow follow-up cannot safely repair all three behaviors without scan-wide event/fork provenance, cache redesign, and real-corpus validation. Since the change is unreleased, restoring the known baseline is the safest containment. This PR does not claim that #2037 is fixed.

Refs #2037

## Verification

- reverted scanner and test blobs are byte-identical to the previously green pre-merge versions; the branch diff is the exact inverse of #2043
- `swift test --filter PiSessionCostScannerTests`: 16/16 passed
- `make check`: zero formatting or lint violations
- full `make test`: 603 selections, all 51 groups first-pass; zero retries, failures, or timeouts
- containment-scoped autoreview: clean
- signed debug bundle: deep strict codesign and Gatekeeper accepted
- source-blind packaged CLI validation: 7/7 passed across cross-file, unique-event, nonlinear-pricing, output-shape, isolation, and production-preservation clauses using only synthetic fixtures
- no dependency, authentication, Keychain, browser, or provider-network changes

target.title: Style settings section footers as leading-aligned footnote captions
target.body:
## Summary

macOS grouped `Form` renders bare section-footer `Text` at body size with trailing alignment. Short one-liners get away with it, but the Advanced pane's four-sentence keychain caption rendered as a large, ragged, right-aligned paragraph.

This adds a shared `SettingsSectionFooter` component (footnote size, secondary color, leading-aligned, full-width) and applies it to every plain-text section footer:

- Advanced: keychain caption + Install CLI status
- General: manual refresh hint
- Menu: agent-sessions footer + cost summary status block
- Quota warnings footer
- Provider settings rows: field/actions/accounts section subtitles

The About pane's centered copyright footer is intentionally left as is.

## Commands run

- `swift build`
- `make check` (SwiftFormat + SwiftLint, 0 violations)
- `make test` (full sharded suite, exit 0)
- Rendered `AdvancedPane` via `NSHostingView` snapshot to verify the caption now reads as a System Settings-style leading footnote caption.
- Codex autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.
